correctness.rationale: For normalized Hardy kernels the Cauchy determinant is a product of pseudohyperbolic pair factors. Each regular ring has explicit circulant Fourier eigenvalues. The cross-product resultant reduces exactly to the gcd-th power of an lcm-frequency binomial. Direct differentiation shows strict phase monotonicity, and an exact log-ratio derivative gives the sharp global bound, with all quantifiers, r=s collisions and m,n=1 checked. The final self-contained checker supplements but does not replace this proof.

originality.rationale: published-finding corpus searches and full comparison against the one-radius sharp Szego orbit theorem establish that the closest known case assumes all points on one radius and explicitly excludes mixed radii. The primary finite Blaschke orbit existence paper yields no determinant optimum, and the 2010 two-circle Euclidean Fekete query states a different, unresolved global problem. No equivalent two-ring pseudohyperbolic phase law or globally sharp coefficient was found. The general D-optimality preprint was accessible only through its abstract and unindexed classical results remain a risk.
residual_risks: The 2026 D-optimality preprint full text was unavailable, so appendix-level coverage could not be exhaustively excluded.
A historical hyperbolic Fekete/reproducing-kernel interpolation paper may state an equivalent two-concentric-orbit phase optimum without searchable terminology.
The all-node Cauchy determinant is classical; the originality judgment concerns the sharp two-ring resultant reduction and complete phase/stability classification, not that identity.

value.rationale: The natural design problem of placing two independently regular families of Hardy interpolation nodes at fixed radii receives a complete phase classification for arbitrary sizes and radii. The lcm/gcd arithmetic structure gives nonobvious phase periodicity and multiplicity; the exactly sharp global log-determinant loss quantifies robustness of the optimal unorthogonalized orbit-frame design. It is a motivated complete classification, not an arbitrary finite sample or classical-identity restatement; it deliberately does not claim the full unrestricted two-circle problem.
